decision.reasoning: I claimed credit for this MOU, so its collapse is a loss against a booked gain — I will spend real capital and accept some domestic cost to defend it rather than let it die on a technicality of an expired deadline. With ratification pending I cannot deliver the deal's central economic term, so I substitute what executive authority actually gives me — waivers, escrow, and posture — to buy time until Congress can be moved. The carrier move and the Israeli reassurance package are the same instrument aimed at both horns of the alliance dilemma: they deter Iranian escalation while giving Jerusalem enough cover that abandonment fears don't drive it to act alone and entrap me.
decision.researchNote: Two-level games (Putnam) most explains this: barred by an unratified Congress from the deal's core economic concession, the executive substitutes unilaterally available waiver and posture instruments to keep the international bargain alive while the domestic ratification game is still being played.
